page: Amazon Web Services m7a.medium is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. The instance features a single dedicated x86_64 physical core and virtual core operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 4 MB L3 cache. Memory is provisioned with 4.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration sets include AVX-512 extensions (f, vnni, bf16) and cryptographic acceleration flags such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes no local storage or bundled GPUs, relying on remote EBS volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-threaded compute efficiency derived from the Zen 4 architecture, achieving top-quartile results in single-core stress-ng (3031.88) and Geekbench single-core (1955.0) metrics, as well as fast bzip3 single-threaded decompression (13.7 GB/sec). However, multi-core throughput and overall aggregate compute capacity scale strictly with the single core, landing multi-threaded and composite system scores such as PassMark CPU (2667.55) in lower performance tiers. Memory throughput records 33.84 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB block reads and 26.46 GB/sec for writes. Redis throughput measures 2.66 million SET operations per second, while static web serving registers 2.2 GB/sec.

As an entry-level general-purpose instance offering dedicated non-burstable CPU execution alongside DDR5 memory, m7a.medium delivers predictable single-thread performance without resource throttling. It is suitable for lightweight production workloads requiring consistent low-latency single-thread execution, including microservices, lightweight web servers, background task runners, development environments, and small-scale caching layers. High-concurrency applications, data-intensive analytics, and local IOPS-dependent databases are constrained by the single-thread ceiling and reliance on network-attached storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.medium is a general-purpose Nitro-based cloud instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Configured with a single dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) clocked at 3.7 GHz, 4.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, and no bundled local storage or GPUs, it provides a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory configuration. Single-threaded performance benchmarks demonstrate strong results, scoring in the top quartile for single-core stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations alongside robust bzip3 decompression rates. However, aggregate throughput is inherently limited by the single-core topology, positioning multi-core compute and overall memory subsystem scores in lower tiers. The instance delivers stable, non-burstable performance suitable for lightweight microservices, modest API backends, task automation, and staging environments where predictable single-thread CPU execution is prioritized over horizontal concurrency or massive parallel throughput.
